cards.text: Paul, called to be an apostle, is writing to everyone in Rome who is loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He just spent a whole chapter on believers who don't agree about food and special days (Romans 14:2, 5). Now he turns to the ones he calls strong, and he says WE, so he's counting himself in.

cards.question: Paul says the strong ought to do what with the shortcomings of the weak?
True or false: Paul tells the strong it's fine to please themselves first.

cards.text: So if it's not about pleasing yourself, who is it about? Paul says each of us should please his neighbor, and friend, I live ALONE on a cookie planet and some days I still manage to get on my own nerves.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says to please your neighbor just to keep him off your back.

cards.text: Then Paul brings out the biggest example there is: even Christ did not please Himself, and Paul quotes Scripture to show it (Psalm 69:9). Meanwhile, friend, I can't let ONE batch cool without sneaking the biggest cookie off the rack for myself.

cards.question: In the Scripture Paul quotes, what has fallen on Christ?

cards.text: Paul just quoted a psalm written long before his day. Now he steps back and says something about EVERYTHING written in the past, the whole stack.

cards.question: Paul says everything that was written in the past was written for our ___.

cards.text: And Paul says that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope. Endurance, friend, is me on the LAST cookie box of a long day, still packing with my mustache while my eyebrows are already asleep.

Then Paul says, may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant them harmony with one another in Christ Jesus. HARMONY, friend, not a group chat where everybody's typing at once and nobody's reading.

cards.question: Paul asks God to grant the believers in Rome harmony, so that with one mind and one voice they may ___ God.

cards.text: Now Paul lands the line this whole section has been building to: accept one another. Not smile, nod and suddenly remember you left something in the oven, friend. ACCEPT.

cards.question: Paul says to accept one another, just as ___ accepted you.
True or false: Paul says accepting one another brings glory to God.

cards.text: Then Paul explains: Christ has become a servant of the circumcised, the Jewish people (Romans 3:29-30), on behalf of God's truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs. And hold on, friend, because Paul says there's a reason for all of it.

cards.question: Paul says Christ became a servant to confirm God's promises, so that who may glorify God for His mercy?

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with Scripture, where David says, "Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name." (Psalm 18:49) And he's not done, friend, he's got verses lined up like cookies on a cooling rack.

cards.question: Paul quotes Scripture AGAIN, and this time the Gentiles are told to rejoice. Rejoice with whom?
And AGAIN Paul quotes Scripture. True or false: this one calls only some of the peoples to praise the Lord.

cards.text: Paul's FOURTH Scripture in a row, friend, and this one's from Isaiah the prophet. He's stacking verses like I stack cookie boxes when a baker's watching.
Isaiah says the Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles (Isaiah 11:10). Jesse was King David's father (Ruth 4:22).

cards.question: In Isaiah's words, what will the Gentiles do in the Root of Jesse?

cards.text: Paul ends with this: may the God of hope fill them with all joy and peace. Hope AGAIN, friend, he keeps circling back to it like I circle the oven in the last ten seconds of the timer, staring through the glass like it owes me money.

cards.question: Paul says, may the God of hope fill the believers in Rome with all joy and peace as they do what?
True or false: Paul says the believers in Rome may overflow with hope by their own strength.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never conveys Paul's positive purpose in Romans 15:2: pleasing one's neighbor is 'for his good, to build him up.' Rejecting 'just to keep him off your back' only rules out a selfish motive and leaves this important detail untaught.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Christ appears for the first time without a simple explanation of who He is. Calling Him 'the biggest example there is' describes His place in Paul's argument, not His identity.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the opening statement, the sentence beginning 'Not smile, nod,' and 'ACCEPT.' It is not the walkthrough's opening card, so it is limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: David is named here for the first time simply as 'David,' without saying who he is. Identifying him as 'King David' does not happen until card 10.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No card states that believers overflow with hope 'by the power of the Holy Spirit.' Marking 'by their own strength' false rules out one source but never teaches the source Paul actually names, leaving out a central detail of Romans 15:13.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
